issue_context.title: Configuration for Blazor WebAssembly
issue_context.body: We provide the config abstraction in the Blazor WebAssembly host, but we don't currently populate it with anything. We should consider what sort of out of the box support we want for configuration in Blazor WebAssembly apps.
comments: I have my WebAssembly project hosted in an ASP.NET core site that's running in docker. I'd like to be able to pass environment variables to the docker container and have them affect the configuration of the WebAssembly on the client.

I created [this package](https://github.com/Darixidor/Blazor.Settings) because I needed access to the environment in a ASP.Net Core hosted situation. In a CDN/plain file hosted situation I'm not sure how you could get the client to understand the variables.

How to set the host configuration?

host.Configuration = ?

Configuration is only a get property there is not set method inside the WebAssemblyHost.

My app is entirely broken by this change. 

I was using @RemiBou implementation [https://remibou.github.io/Configuring-a-Blazor-app/](https://remibou.github.io/Configuring-a-Blazor-app/) but it doesn't work anymore.

UPDATE:
Blazor now support configuration files out of the box please see @danroth27 post below: 

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/18675#issuecomment-612531194

OLD BUT WORKS:

I just resolved the issue. 

There are other people asking for this and there is no example or documentation on this.

I will left here the solution after 2 wasted days crashing on all errors and working around with this.

This
`WebAssemblyHostBuilder builder = WebAssemblyHostBuilder.CreateDefault(args);`

Holds the configuration builder which enables to insert a configuration file.

`//Example`
`builder.Configuration.AddJsonFile(//your config file were ever its located or loaded)`

Take note that DON'T BUILD THE CONFIGURATION file it will throw an error:

```
//Don't do this
builder.Configuration.Build();
```

Let

`WebAssemblyHost host = builder.Build();`

Build the configuration file for you.

Then the configuration file now will be loaded and available from

`var configuration = host.Services.GetRequiredService<IConfiguration>();`

Or

```
[Inject]
IConfiguration Configuration { get; set; }
```

Hope this helps someone.
